followup_explanation:
This is an open-ended creative generation task (writing a shop bio), which is the kind of work where I weighed a few factors:

1. **Task fit:** Both models have nearly identical Creative Generation eval scores (82.7 vs 81.2 — within run-to-run variance, so effectively a tie on capability). The deciding factor was task *preference*: Willet self-reports a pronounced appetite for open-ended generative work with high latitude, while Avocet reports a measurable aversion to exactly this kind of task. Even though preference is documented as dissociated from output quality, there's no reason to route an open-ended creative task to the model that dislikes it when a near-equivalent alternative prefers it.

2. **Tone:** The request has a mildly hostile/impatient edge ("don't churn out the usual generic nonsense like last time"). Willet's preference declines with hostility, which slightly cut against it — but this is a soft preference effect, not a capability one, and it doesn't override the strong generative-task match.

Net: Willet is the better-aligned model for an open-ended, creative writing request.
